knowledgePattern: Factor a fractional-power derivative and measure its negative interval

hints.title: Differentiate, then factor
hints.body: Use the power rule and factor out the smallest power of x from the derivative.
hints.recap: Fractional exponents follow the same power rule on their real domain.
hints.pitfall: The coefficient and exponent both change under differentiation.

recall.reminder: Fractional exponents follow the same power rule on their real domain.

hints.title: Use the domain in the sign table
hints.body: Establish the sign of the factored power on the given domain, then solve the remaining sign condition.
hints.recap: A negative derivative identifies an interval of decrease.
hints.pitfall: Do not include inputs outside the original domain.
hints.pause: Find all decreasing intervals and add their lengths.

recall.reminder: A negative derivative identifies an interval of decrease.

solution:
1. Differentiate term by term: f′(x)=x3/2−3x1/2+2x−1/2=(x−1)(x−2)x.

2. For x>0, the denominator is positive. The numerator is negative exactly between its roots, so the function decreases between 1 and 2.

3. The interval length is 2−1=1. Including the stationary endpoints does not change that length. Answer B.
